To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the constitutive activity of H2R is species-specific with the highest activity being exhibited by cH2R and the ligand selectivity of H2R isoforms is also species-specific.
the constitutive activity of the H2R species varies, and that the H2R ligands show species-specific selectivity profiles.
cH2R is more active in the basal state and more sensitive to ligand-induced activation than hH2R.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of species-dependent H2R properties.
the identification of the molecular determinants responsible for the observed differences in the properties of H2Rs of various species.
the molecular mechanisms of constitutive activity and ligand selectivity in H2R variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hH2R is the prototypic H2R species variant, and the cH2Rs are more closely related to the gpH2R than to the rH2R.
the cH2Rs show a higher basal activity compared with h, gp, and r H2Rs.
there are species differences with respect to the extent of constitutive activity and ligand selectivity of H2Rs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H2R species exhibit differences in constitutive activity and ligand selectivity that may be of relevance in vivo.
cH2R and hH2R are more alike with respect to constitutive activity and ligand selectivity than hH2R and gpH2R.
H2R ligand selectivity and H2R species selectivity are related to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H2R species variant cH2R has the highest basal and ligand-induced activity and that there are ligand-dependent differences in the conformations of the H2R variants.
the constitutive activity and the ligand selectivity of H2R are not conserved among the four H2R species studied.
H2R species differ in their constitutive activity and ligand selectivity.
